draft.title: Senge's learning organisation
card: Peter Senge described a learning organisation as a business that keeps learning and adapts as conditions change. He named five disciplines that help it do this.
seeing the business as a whole, where each part affects the others. Personal mastery is each person's commitment to keep building their own skills.
the assumptions people hold about how the business and its market work. A learning organisation questions these assumptions instead of taking them for granted.
a shared vision is a future that everyone in the business wants to work towards. Team learning is when groups share ideas and learn together, not only as individuals.
draft.remember: A learning organisation keeps learning through five disciplines, so it can adapt as conditions change.

a.q: Managers at a bakery in Geelong ask staff to test their belief that customers only want cheap bread. Which of Senge's disciplines is this?
a.why: The belief about customers is an assumption about how the market works, so questioning it is mental models. Systems thinking is tempting, but it is about seeing how the parts of the whole business affect each other, not testing an assumption.
a.clue: Which discipline is about assumptions people hold?

b.q: Sam runs a Ballarat building firm. The sales, design and site teams meet to find how a late design change affects costs on site and in the office. Which discipline is mainly at work?
b.why: The teams are looking at how one change affects other parts of the whole business, which is systems thinking. Mental models is tempting, but nothing here questions an assumption. The focus is on links between parts.
b.clue: The focus is on how the parts of the business affect each other.
